reasoning_traces.think:
The PRF establishes relevance as a latent variable governed by probabilistic laws. It begins with the Probability Ranking Principle, where documents are ranked according to P(r|q,d). BM25 arises as a tractable approximation to this principle, using term frequency and inverse document frequency to estimate relevance. BM25F extends this by combining multiple independent relevance streams, enabling richer document modeling. The framework's strength lies in its ability to unify diverse retrieval strategies under a common probabilistic foundation. Its failure mode occurs when term distributions are too sparse or when relevance assumptions break down due to semantic drift. Dualities emerge in how BM25 balances term frequency and document length normalization, while its extension to BM25F allows for meta-data integration. The framework supports both supervised and unsupervised learning paradigms through relevance feedback mechanisms.
